Quetzaltenango is a charming town founded in 1524. It is located in the highlands among volcanoes. Quetzaltenango is a base for excursions into the mountains, to hot springs and to villages of local artisans. Volcano ascents begin here. The city also attracts people who want to study Spanish and volunteers who help local Maya communities develop.

Quetzaltenango lies in southwestern Guatemala, in a highland region at an altitude of 2333 meters. It is the country's second most populous city. For a time during the first half of the 19th century, it served as the capital of the state of Los Altos.

## Exploring the Surroundings of Quetzaltenango

### Quetzaltenango — A Base for New Excursions!

The city is a convenient departure point for exploring Guatemala. Nearby, you can visit one of the colorful local villages or enjoy the hot springs. Products made by local artisans are popular with visitors, especially homespun woolen goods and traditional clothing. In the city, visit Quetzaltenango's central square and stroll through the main park, which offers a wonderful panorama of the surrounding mountains and volcanoes.

King George Island plays an important role in international scientific research. It is home to polar research stations where scientists study the climate, atmosphere, glaciers, ocean and distinctive Antarctic ecosystems. Thanks to its relatively accessible location, the island serves as one of the main departure points for expeditions to Antarctica.

Traveling to King George Island offers an unusual perspective on Antarctica. There are no conventional cities, busy streets or extensive tourist facilities. Instead, you encounter boundless expanses, the austere beauty of the polar wilderness, silence broken only by seabird calls and the sense of being at the edge of the inhabited world.

Even so, reaching the island is not easy: journeys depend on the weather, sea conditions and the availability of air connections. This remoteness makes the trip especially exciting, turning it into a true polar adventure.

King George Island is a place where science meets wilderness and travelers come face to face with the grandeur of Antarctica.

Quito is situated in an Andean valley at an altitude of 2850 m. The old town preserves colonial architecture, churches and monasteries, while the modern part of the capital spreads among mountains and volcanic ranges.

From Quito, it is easy to continue to the equator. North of the city stands a monument marking zero latitude, with views of the Pululahua crater nearby.

South of Quito begins the Avenue of the Volcanoes. In this direction lie Cotopaxi, at 5897 m, high-altitude natural areas and routes to Quilotoa Crater Lake.

## Cobán — The Center of Alta Verapaz

### Cobán — A Maya Stronghold!

Cobán is a starting point for excursions through the magnificent natural landscapes of Alta Verapaz. The city is developing so quickly that even visitors returning after just a year are surprised by how much it has changed. At the entrance to the city, a sign reads: "Bienvenidos Coban, Ciudad Imptrial". It commemorates the city charter granted in 1538 by Emperor Charles himself. The city was once the center of Tezulutlán (Tierra de Guerra, or "Land of War"), a Maya stronghold.

The first German settlers arrived here in the 19th century, bringing elements of German mountain-town architecture. Many picturesque estates and residences of the local elite surround the city.

## The Variety of Experiences in Cobán

### Experience Cobán's Atmosphere!

The city still retains the atmosphere of a small German town, with numerous Protestant and Catholic churches. There are many German-style cafés and restaurants, as well as places serving local cuisine. Coffee lovers call Cobán Guatemala's capital of this strong, invigorating and aromatic drink. The city is surrounded by coffee plantations, where visitors can learn how coffee beans are grown and processed and take a guided tour.
